messages:
nora: Hi @people-ops — my partner and I welcomed a baby last week. I'm thinking about taking intermittent parental leave for the next 3 months (a few days here and there). What's the best way to file and how does payroll handle intermittent days?

mira (People Ops): Congrats Nora! :tada: Intermittent leave is supported. Best flow: 1) Create a leave case in the HR portal and select 'intermittent/partial' 2) Add the expected window and a note describing cadence (e.g., 2-3 days/month) 3) Upload the birth docs when you have them. Payroll handles pay on a per-pay-period basis; submit leave days in the portal timesheet so payroll can process each period.

sam (manager): From the team side, can you flag blackout weeks (major launches) so we avoid gaps? Also please add a short on-call backup plan.
ora: Yes — I'll block 2026-10-12 to 2026-10-19 as "no leave" for the release, and put a 2-person backup for on-call.

mira (People Ops): Quick notes: benefits remain active on approved leave days. If you expect many intermittent days, consider a phased return request (reduced hours) instead — it can be easier for payroll and managers. Also, upload docs within 14 days of filing to avoid processing delays.

people-ops-bot: reminder: "Upload birth docs to HR portal and record intermittent leave days in timesheet each pay period to ensure correct pay processing."

nora: One more Q — I need a lactation room access card and occasional flexible schedule for appointments. How do I request those?
mira (People Ops): For lactation room — facilities handles key/cards. I'll open a ticket and cc Facilities; expect confirmation in 2 business days. For flexible schedule, add it in the notes of your leave case and we'll coordinate manager approval.

sam (manager): Thanks Mira. Nora — ping me once you file and I'll approve the coverage plan.

nora: Filing now, will tag you. Appreciate the quick help! :heart:
